sections.html:
Grandview is a south-side suburb of Kansas City with roughly 26,000 people, in Jackson County along Interstate 49. A post office has operated under the Grandview name since 1889, and the city incorporated on February 6, 1912. Harry Truman grew up working on the family farm here, and many service members lived in town while stationed at Richards-Gebaur Air Force Base, which closed in 1994.

Grandview was once a rail town and later a bedroom suburb. Population climbed from 6,027 in 1960 to 24,502 in 1980, then held near 25,000 for decades. The city covers 14.73 square miles. The ZIP code is 64030, and phone area codes are 816 and 975. The I-49 outer roads were converted to two-way traffic in a $15 million project that finished in November 2022, which changed how drivers reach homes and shops along the corridor.

Grandview leans toward renters: fewer than half of its homes are owner-occupied. If you own a rental, or inherited one, read the city's registration rules before you set a closing date.

The 2020 census counted 11,606 housing units in Grandview, and 8.1% stood empty. About 86.7% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Median age is 35.2, so many buyers here are first-time owners looking at starter prices near the $188,500 median.

Grandview requires an inspection of rental and non-owner-occupied dwellings before a new tenant can move in. The Board of Aldermen approved the ordinance on January 22, 2019, and inspections take place between occupancies.

The inspection certificate fee is $20 per dwelling and must be paid before the dwelling can be occupied. Dwellings also register every year, with registrations due December 31 for the following calendar year. The fee is $12 per unit for 1 to 50 units, and it steps down per unit for larger portfolios. To schedule an inspection, call (816) 316-4819 or (816) 316-4817. Payment questions go to (816) 316-4823.

If you rent the house out, a buyer who wants to keep tenants will ask whether this year's registration is paid and a current inspection certificate is on file. A vacant house between tenants is easier to show to a buyer who will live there.

  • Pull your registration receipt and your latest inspection certificate before you list.
  • Check the city's rental map to see whether the address falls in the registration area.
  • Ask Building Services whether a lapse in registration carries a fee.

sections.h2: Jackson County assessments and tax bills
sections.html:
For a Grandview house, three jobs sit with Jackson County: valuing the property, sending the tax bill and keeping the deed record. Visit the Assessment Department at 1300 Washington Street in Kansas City or phone (816) 881-1330.

Homes are assessed at 19% of market value. Collections staff have no power to change an assessed value, a levy rate or a bill. Think the value is wrong? Collect comparable sales and ask Assessment about an informal review. Do this before you list, since a lower value also helps the next owner.

Statements arrive in November, with payment due December 31. Checks are payable to the Jackson County Collector and can be dropped off at Grandview City Hall as long as the bill is not three or more years past due. Credit and debit cards are accepted. Many bills go to mortgage servicers with escrow accounts, so ask your lender for the amount it paid. Senior residents may qualify for an extended payment plan, and the city's tax page lists (816) 881-3232 for details.

sections.h2: Recording charges at the Jackson County Recorder of Deeds
sections.html:
A deed filed in Jackson County costs $23 for its first page and $3 for each page after. Out of that $23, $8 is passed to the State of Missouri (Local Preservation Fund, State Surveyor Fund, State Housing Trust Fund and County Recorder's Fund) and $15 is kept by the county. Card payments at the counter add a 2.75% processing fee on the whole transaction. If you mail a check, make it out to the Recorder of Deeds Department.

  • Releases and assignments add $5 for each additional affected number.
  • Copies run $2 for page one and $1 per later page, and certifying a document adds $1.
  • Ask your title company to confirm who submits the deed for recording, and whether the fee comes out of your proceeds.

Most of Grandview belongs to the Grandview C-4 School District, which runs six elementary schools, one middle school, Grandview Senior High School and an alternative school. A small portion falls in Hickman Mills C-1. The Mid-Continent Public Library has a branch in town.

Recent additions buyers may mention include a National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration office, Southpointe Business Park, and a 400-unit expansion of Grand Summit Apartments. The city also reports renovation of three major retail centers.

sections.h2: Listing, landlord sale or direct purchase?
sections.html:
The choice depends on whether the house is empty, tenant-occupied or in need of work, and on how soon you want to be done.

  • A traditional listing works best on a move-in ready house. It brings showings and the buyer's own inspection.
  • A sale with tenants in place can go to an investor who values the lease. Share the rental registration and the inspection history up front.
  • A direct purchase by a cash buyer can close without repairs, and the house goes to the buyer as it stands.

Whichever way you go, ask for the net figure after taxes, any lien payoff, title charges and recording. A written offer that spells out those items is easier to compare than a headline number.

sections.h2: Steps to close a Grandview sale
sections.html: Before you talk to buyers, pull together the tax bill or your lender's escrow statement, the rental registration receipt and inspection certificate if the house is a rental, and any loan payoff figure. Then pick the route that suits the house and collect offers in writing. Once you sign one, the title company orders the title search, prorates the tax bill, pays off liens and files the deed with the Jackson County Recorder of Deeds. Ask the buyer how soon they can close and whether they pay your closing costs. A cash sale cuts out the buyer's loan approval and appraisal, which are the steps most likely to stretch a closing date.

faqs.q: Does Grandview require an inspection when a house is sold?
faqs.a: The city's building pages describe inspections for new construction and for rentals between tenants. If you sell a rental, the buyer who rents it out will need the registration and a fresh inspection certificate before a new tenant moves in.

faqs.q: How much is the rental inspection certificate in Grandview?
faqs.a: $20 per dwelling. It must be paid before the dwelling can be occupied, and the city will not issue the certificate until payment is made.

faqs.q: Where do I pay real estate tax on a Grandview house?
faqs.a: To the Jackson County Collector, by December 31. The county mails statements in November, and the city accepts payment at City Hall while the bill is under three years past due.

faqs.q: What will recording the deed cost on a Grandview sale?
faqs.a: $23 for page one and $3 for each page after it at the Jackson County Recorder of Deeds. Paying by card adds 2.75%.
Yes, slowly. Federal estimates show 26,653 residents in mid-2025, up 1.7% from a 2020 base of 26,208.
